extracted.intended_audience: educated readers, students and practitioners concerned with the relation between religion and science (scientists, clergy, philosophers, and general readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and methodological guidance for assessing, comparing, and reconciling conflicting religious and scientific beliefs; recommends attitudes and procedures for fair critical judgment and mutual understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare like opinions and isolate common element
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare all opinions of the same genus; set aside the special and concrete elements in which such opinions disagree; observe what remains after the discordant constituents have been eliminated; find the abstract expression which holds true throughout divergent modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method is to compare all opinions of the same kind, eliminate their concrete disagreements, and identify the remaining common, abstract truth. This helps locate the 'soul of truth' within apparently erroneous creeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt an impartial attitude—expect partial truth in opponents
rubrics_metrics.description: Be ever ready to suspect that the convictions we entertain are not wholly right, and that the adverse convictions are not wholly wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting beliefs be determined by accidental birth or epoch and avoid the error of entire and contemptuous negation. Love truth more than victory; cultivate candour and willingness to see how opponents perceive things.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek mutual understanding rather than wholesale rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive to understand what it is that leads our opponents to think as they do; aim to supplement the portion of truth we have found with the portion found by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extremes of undue submission and undue rebellion. Rather than charging opponents with stupidity or dishonesty, go over to their side to discover the aspect of the question you have missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat science by its nature and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge Science by itself: it is an organized, growing mass of facts established by examination, verification, and the continuous exposing and rejecting of error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize science as a higher development of common knowledge—subject results to searching examination; value daily verification of scientific predictions and practical triumphs of arts guided by science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the religious sentiment as real and consequential
rubrics_metrics.description: Religious ideas are almost universal and often independently evolved; the existence and omnipresence of a religious sentiment is a fact that must be accounted for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if religious creeds are erroneous in parts, their vitality and universality suggest they contain an element of truth. Students of science must inquire into the origin and function of the religious sentiment rather than ignore it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the limits of scientific knowledge—leave room for religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive knowledge cannot fill the whole region of possible thought; at the uttermost reach of discovery a question 'What lies beyond?' will always remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because inquiry always meets further unknowns, there will always be a place for a mode of thought whose subject matter passes the sphere of experience—i.e., a place for Religion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical and comparative evidence when judging widespread beliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: The universality, independent evolution, and persistence of certain religious elements across races and ages provide probabilistic grounds that these elements are not purely accidental or priestly inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philological and comparative-historical evidence weaken hypotheses that religions are artificially contrived; the repeated independent emergence and survival of elements imply a deep-seated source in human experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dismissing a domain because of its corruptions or follies
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortcomings in advocates of Religion (or Science) do not tell essentially against what is advocated; both domains must be judged by their own merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let the corruptions or folly of some proponents justify wholesale rejection of the domain. Science and Religion should both be allowed the reverence their respective merits warrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect harmony between Religion and Science
rubrics_metrics.description: If both religion and science have bases in reality, then between them there must be a fundamental harmony rather than absolute and everlasting opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject Manichean opposition; seek the hidden agreement and regard each as a constituent of the larger whole. Both claims should be recognized as standing for truths not to be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat religion as a legitimate subject for scientific study without prejudice
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who contemplate the universe from the scientific point of view must learn to see Religion as a constituent of the great whole and treat it as a subject of science with no more prejudice than any other reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific study of religion should be undertaken impartially. Likewise, the religiously-minded should regard scientific findings as a legitimate constituent of understanding the universe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain intellectual humility and balance between submission and rebellion
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the extremes of implicit submission to authority and contemptuous negation; cultivate candour and readiness to revise beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This temper prevents unthinking acceptance of inherited beliefs and the opposite fashionable wholesale rejection; it encourages measured criticism and the search for shared truths.
